question.text: What is the key difference between a Gold ETF and a Gold Fund of Funds (FoF)?

answer.text: Gold ETFs invest in physical gold while Gold FoFs invest in gold mining company stocks
Gold ETFs require a demat account and are traded on exchanges, while Gold FoFs invest in Gold ETFs and can be purchased without a demat account
Gold FoFs have lower expense ratios than Gold ETFs
Gold ETFs offer SIP facility while Gold FoFs do not

explanation.text: The Logic: Gold ETFs are exchange-traded funds that hold physical gold and trade on stock exchanges like shares — investors transact in them through a broker on the exchange, which generally requires a demat account. Gold Fund of Funds (FoFs) are mutual fund schemes whose underlying holdings are typically Gold ETF units; because they are bought and sold as ordinary mutual fund units (via the AMC or distributor route), investors can purchase them without a demat account, including through SIP. The Trap: "Gold ETFs invest in physical gold while Gold FoFs invest in gold mining stocks" confuses Gold FoFs with gold sector/mining equity funds — Gold FoFs invest in gold-backed instruments, not mining equities. "Gold FoFs have lower expense ratios" is the opposite of reality: an FoF route adds an extra layer of costs on top of the underlying Gold ETF's TER. "Gold ETFs offer SIP while Gold FoFs do not" reverses how the products are actually accessed — SIP is more naturally available in the FoF wrapper. Note: The specific framing that Gold FoFs invest in Gold ETFs and can be purchased without a demat account is not explicitly laid out as a single statement in the cited NISM Series V-A workbook pages. The explanation above is given as general industry knowledge of how Gold ETFs and Gold FoFs are structured and accessed in the Indian mutual fund market.
